searches.note: Twenty three searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's, and five left unspent. One Marqués de Griñón search was refused before it ran because it named three newspaper domains the tool cannot reach, and is counted all the same. Two were restricted to boe.es (the ratification of 2003 and Ley 24/2003) and are read as primary through their summaries; one was restricted to the co-operative's own domain, vinostomillar.es, and found its cellar page but no sheet of Tomillar Airén. The rest went to the open web with the author's sources blocked where they would only have repeated themselves (the houses' own domains, Grandes Pagos, the Real Academia, Decanter, wein.plus, the regional tourism body, the Sommeliers Choice Awards, FENAVIN, Vinos Cutanda, and writers' own sites by turns). The two shared searches are the history of DO La Mancha (Ayuso and Virgen de las Viñas) and the ageing terms of Ley 24/2003 (Félix Solís and Ayuso). One fetch tried, of vinostomillar.es, refused because the host is not allowed here, and not retried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the decrees (the BOE for the two pagos and the ageing law), then to independent accounts of each house's dates and people, then to merchants' and guides' sheets of each wine for the blend, the months in oak and the glass, with the author's sources blocked so that an independent account could be heard.

Where the sheets disagreed and none was primary, the figure was cut or hedged as the house's; where a fact the plan asked for and the author had left out was now borne out twice (the hunting estate of Dehesa del Carrizal, its first harvests made at Valdepusa), it was added.

tested: The pago's year, with the family and Grandes Pagos blocked: CataDelVino, Mr Vinos and Wine Paths give the regional order of 19 July 2002; the BOE (BOE-A-2003-5034) gives Orden APA/519/2003 of 21 February 2003, published on 11 March 2003, ratifying the regulation of that order. So 2002 stands, and the 2003 that the author called European is the Spanish ministry's ratification. Changed.

Carlos Falcó: 20 March 2020 in Madrid, aged 83, of Covid, by Spanish Wikipedia, El Español and Madridiario; born in Seville in 1937 by Spanish Wikipedia; Louvain and then Davis by Spanish Wikipedia; the estate inherited from his grandfather by one press account with the author's Academia. Borne out; 1959 rests on the Academia and the family (open).

Drip irrigation in 1974 and the first Cabernet of 1982: Spanish Wikipedia for 1974; three accounts for the first commercial vintage of 1982 from the Cabernet planted in 1974. Borne out. Peynaud's role, dated 1974 by one and 1982 by another, stays out, and a later consultant met in the results is living and not named.

The blend and the oak of Emeritus, with Vinos Cutanda and espagne-gourmet blocked: El Corte Inglés's sheet of 2021 (45 per cent Cabernet, 42 Syrah, 13 Petit Verdot, twenty four months in French oak), Wine.com's of 1998 (51, 35 and 14, thirteen months and more in new French oak), Vinello (83, 11 and 6, twenty four months). Syrah is often second and Cabernet sometimes under half: changed. The label's EMERITVS borne out by a merchant's listing of the 1997.

The traps: Marqués de Griñón Rioja borne out by a listing of a Rioja Clásico under the name; the house rules hold: nobody living named, no price, no score, British, no dash. The Calificada explanation was wrong against the Codex's own records and is changed.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment's prose; the read together agent adds those it judges living to people.json. Carlos Falcó (1937 to 2020) is dead and named with his dates, borne out by Spanish Wikipedia, El Español and Madridiario. Described, never named, for want of dates in two sources: Félix Solís Fernández and Leonor Yáñez, the founders of 1952 (the house keeps its name Félix Solís); Fermín Ayuso Roig, the founder of 1947; the fifteen or seventeen founders of Virgen de las Viñas. Émile Peynaud is dead but his role at Valdepusa is dated two ways and stays out; a later consultant met in the results is already on people.json. A critic met in the results is already on people.json and is no source here.
swapNote: No swap was proposed by the author, and the refuter proposes none. Marqués de Griñón's Emeritus and Dehesa del Carrizal are two of the plateau's pagos, the first by the regional order of 2002 and the second by the order of 2006; Félix Solís is the Valdepeñas house of Viña Albali, its brand dated to 1962; Bodegas Ayuso's Estola is the aged red of 1965 the house and the DO's own page put first; Virgen de las Viñas stands under the thin region rule, a growers' co-operative of 1961 whose Tomillar Airén is borne out by three listings and said to be what it is. Dehesa del Carrizal's Cabernet Sauvignon is made under that name by the estate's own page and was its first wine, from the 1989 harvest, so Finca Antigua, the plan's fallback, is not needed.
planNotes: marques-de-grinon: answered. The decree decides 2002: the regional order of 19 July 2002, ratified by Orden APA/519/2003 of 21 February 2003 (BOE of 11 March 2003). The blend is taught as Cabernet leading with Syrah and Petit Verdot, the shares moving widely; Falcó's dates by the Academia, Spanish Wikipedia and two newspapers; no living member of the family named; Valdepusa said to be a DO Pago of its own, not DO La Mancha.

felix-solis: answered. Félix Solís, trading as Félix Solís Avantis; 1952 by the company and three secondary accounts; the family's story told from the company's own history; the label Viña Albali Gran Reserva, DO Valdepeñas, borne out by the group's shop and Disenzo; Valdepeñas said to be a DO of its own.

ayuso: answered. 1947, 1961 and 1965 by the DO La Mancha's own page, the London Drinks Guide and De Bodega en Bodega besides the house; the first Reserva hedged as the house's claim; the founder is named in those sources but his dates nowhere, so he is described.

virgen-de-las-vinas: answered. 1961 by La Voz de Tomelloso and Turismo de Ciudad Real besides the author's two; the label Tomillar Airén, DO La Mancha, by Infovinos, De Bodega en Bodega and Uno de Copas; the merger of 2026 told nowhere in the record; the record says it is a co-operative.

dehesa-del-carrizal: answered. The pago's year 2006 by the BOE; the founding planting of 1987; the Cabernet Sauvignon made under that name, with Colección Privada a selection above it in chosen years. The plan's why calls it a hunting estate, which the author left out for want of a source: Proensa and a second account bear it out, and the story now says so, so the why stands.

BOE: Ley 24/2003 de la Viña y del Vino

codexInTension.where: .scripts/regions/fragments, the La Mancha producers line for Félix Solís
codexInTension.says: the cheap aged Cencibel that taught the world the words Reserva and Gran Reserva
codexInTension.read: A price word the Flagships tab refuses, and a claim no source read makes; the flagship record says only that the Gran Reserva carries the ageing category to a wide public.

codexInTension.where: .scripts/regions/fragments, the La Mancha producers line for Virgen de las Viñas
codexInTension.says: one of the largest wineries in Europe
codexInTension.read: The press calls it the largest wine co-operative of Europe in 2022 and of the world after the merger of March 2026: a ranking that moves with the year, which the flagship record leaves out.

sources.title: La Voz de Tomelloso: the co-operative at sixty years

codexInTension.says: for decades the best-known aged red of DO La Mancha
codexInTension.read: A ranking no source read makes; the flagship record says the bottle the house is known by.

codexNote: Reported, never edited: REGIONS, WINE_PRODUCERS and the Codex's question banks stay as they are. The Codex's own Spanish records place the Vino de Pago above DOCa in the statute, which is why both of this group's Calificada explanations were changed rather than the Codex. None of the five houses is in WINE_PRODUCERS.
